newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Mexico, Mugabe attack U.S. over Cuba, U.N. chief.
newsitem.headline: Mexico, Mugabe attack U.S. over Cuba, U.N. chief.

text.p: Zimbabwe's President Robert Mugabe and Mexico's foreign minister on Sunday criticised the United States for passing a law seeking to punish companies dealing with Cuba.
Mugabe, chairing a session of a Group of 15 (G-15) trade conference, also attacked Washington for opposing the re-election of U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali.

"We feel that it is wrong for a state to transfer its hatred of another country and make it affect its relationship with a third country, and force countries with a relationship with Cuba to stop relating with it," he said.
"The United States of America has always sought to impose its will on everybody else. They are passing this to us as a general attitude and that is what we must resist," Mugabe said.

Speaking at the same session, Mexican Foreign Minister Jose Angel Gurria Trevino urged fellow G-15 members -- Algeria, Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Egypt, India, Indonesia, Jamaica, Malaysia, Nigeria, Senegal, Peru, Venezuela, Yugoslavia and Zimbabwe -- to consider its example in opposing the controversial U.S. law on Cuba.

"Mexico has already passed a law of its own as an antidote for the unilateral actions taken by the United States of America and its discriminatory practices with Cuba which is affecting relations of other countries," he said.
